model_evidence: Author-defined conceptual anatomy model; not a measured MRI/CT segmentation or an independently verified anatomical reconstruction.
model_notes: Names and source-defined laterality are preserved. Anatomical directions of the world coordinate axes are not independently verified.

Mesh objects use the source author's original viewport modifier stack in the pinned Blender runtime. Both evaluated geometry and original base vertices/polygons are retained. Curves keep the source bevel and resolution; no project-created modifier is added.
Model curve thickness is illustrative and cannot be used as a vessel or nerve diameter measurement.
Retained source object transforms may include source-authored reflections. The project adds no new mirroring, anatomical registration, refinement or inferred structure partitions.
scope_notes: Independent 3D source model without an original image volume. Compare another native atlas in its own panel; no correspondence is implied.
Named artery and venous models retain supplied extents and branch definitions; they do not establish individual branching anatomy or population variant prevalence.
Source CN I-XII objects may include extracranial context; cisternal, canalicular and extracranial segments have not been independently partitioned.
Source labels for foramina and canals include two-point locator objects, not hole surfaces. They are not included in this surface catalogue. Individual bones provide conceptual skull-base context.
Falx and tentorial model sheets are dural context, not arachnoid membranes or segmented cistern boundaries.
No disease, lesion, clinical decision function, image fusion or blanket expert review is included.

Additional source nuclear, commissural, limbic and pituitary models retain their original object hierarchy. The combined lentiform object overlaps separate source components; surface extent and low-order model shape do not establish individual microscopic anatomy.

This configuration preserves the earlier 350 source objects unchanged and adds 48 explicitly audited source objects. The source file contains a whole-body model; this bounded inventory covers the current intracranial and cranial-context scope, not every source object or every human anatomical structure.

Whole-body, dedicated eye/ear/dental/maxillofacial additions, source text/locator objects and unlabelled helper curves are excluded by the recorded source-object audit. Original source-defined surfaces may overlap.

Telencephalic white matter is a broad tissue model, not a new named tract. Native named sinus surfaces are author-defined skull cavity models, not CT intensities, inferred air masks or new neural tissue.

teaching_sequences.objective: Identify the modeled carotid, cerebral and communicating arteries in one continuous exploration.
teaching_sequences.instruction: Begin with the entire visible arterial context. Select each target, rotate the view, then use Focus selected for local inspection. Return to Full model view before comparing sides.

steps.prompt: Trace the source left internal carotid model and compare it with the adjacent cerebral branch models.
steps.question: Which source object is selected, and which neighboring arterial names can you identify?
steps.answer: The source object is the left internal carotid artery. Keep the anterior cerebral and posterior communicating labels visible while tracing its modeled course; the package does not partition named carotid segments.

steps.prompt: View the midline communicating model from above and below.
steps.question: Which named communicating object is represented between the paired anterior cerebral models?
steps.answer: The source labels this object anterior communicating artery. Its original author Mirror modifier is retained; this is source-authored model geometry, not a newly inferred mirrored vessel.

steps.prompt: Compare the left posterior communicating model with the ipsilateral carotid and posterior cerebral models.
steps.question: Which three source objects provide this local communicating-artery context?
steps.answer: Left posterior communicating artery, left internal carotid artery and left posterior cerebral artery. Their model labels support a spatial exercise; they do not establish an individual fetal-type configuration.

steps.prompt: Return to the whole model and inspect the corresponding right-side source object.
steps.question: Does the existence of two model objects demonstrate a normal population prevalence or prove perfect anatomical symmetry?
steps.answer: No. These are source-authored left and right objects in one model. A variant frequency requires an independently defined normal cohort and measurements.

teaching_sequences.evidence_limit: Author-defined source models in one native XYZ space. The shapes are educational models, not individual angiography, measured lumen diameters or population frequencies. No MRI alignment is supplied.

teaching_sequences.title: MCA source segments and cortical branches
teaching_sequences.objective: Follow the named MCA segment models and distinguish segment labels from regional branch groups.
teaching_sequences.instruction: Inspect M1, the insular M2 model and M3 in sequence, then compare the temporal and parietal branch groups. Keep the full selected context visible while rotating.

steps.prompt: Locate the source left M1 object before following the next modeled segment.
steps.question: Which MCA segment does the source name specify?
steps.answer: Left middle cerebral artery M1. The label is supplied by the model author; the software does not calculate a segment boundary from vessel shape.

steps.prompt: Compare the insular M2 source object with M1 and the next M3 model.
steps.question: Which source wording distinguishes this model from a single unbranched tube?
steps.answer: The author calls it insular branches of the middle cerebral artery (M2-segment). A grouped source object can contain branching geometry; one selectable object is not necessarily one vessel branch.

steps.prompt: Follow the source-defined M3 object without changing the model coordinate space.
steps.question: Is an M4 subdivision independently selectable in this delivered selection?
steps.answer: No. M1, M2 and M3 are named here; the selected source inventory has regional temporal and parietal branch groups, but no separately labeled M4 object.
